evidence: Requirement-to-criterion mapping substantially covers the ask: login/identity -> hro_gate_render/hro_accounts; shared durable creation -> hro_gate_shared/hro_readback/hro_restart; seed -> seven hro_seed_* rows; IDs and creation -> hro_req_identity/hro_offer_identity/hro_duplicate_identity and unusual-ID lifecycle rows; validation -> P2 rows; composition/bands -> hro_compensation_breakdown/hro_intrinsic/hro_annual/hro_runrate/hro_basis/hro_bands; roles, dual control and budgets -> P5/P6 rows; approval/revision/rescission effects, history, vesting, referral and concurrency -> P4/P7/P8/P9 rows; dashboard -> hro_dashboard; accessibility, themes, recovery and states -> Polish; visual quality -> six anchored Visual rows. Shared flows are allowed by Internal Quality Checks!E27; no finding is based merely on bundled rules. Two uncovered promises remain. (1) .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md:260-263 explicitly requires replacing the active grant with revised "unit count, fair value and strike price". .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:443 checks revised units, original instant, historical status/cancellations and zero-unit removal, but never the replacement grant fair/strike values. hro_revision_lineage at :398 checks the six economic fields of the OFFER; hro_grant at :362 checks units/date/schedule; neither establishes replacement GRANT prices. P4 in functional/prompt.md changes fair/strike on the offer but supplies no scored comparison of these replacement-grant prices. (2) .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md:370-383 and :401-402 requires all action identity/permissions to come from session and all documented optional claims to be ignored. .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:605 applies claimedActorId/claimedRole/claimedTier only to approval; :614 checks approval economic claims; :623 checks only claimedClawbackCents/claimedCancelledUnits on rescission. functional/prompt.md:49 explicitly limits the claim controls to those approval and rescission bodies. Revision has no claim probe, and nonapproval creation/rescission have no forged identity/role probe. Ordinary wrong-role controls (:290/:299), anonymous-family controls and normal audit actor checks do not exercise a caller adding these claims. Hash verification found zero mismatches across all 69 frozen task/rules files. The raw-evidence-index.json was absent when read; no browser, mutation or configured judge run was performed for this row. These are bounded source coverage counterexamples, not an empirical score or a claim about the golden. Shared template implementation constraints were distinguished from task-specific browser criteria; this finding does not ask for source-reading or a database-engine browser probe.
counterexample: Broken app A correctly revises all six offer fields and computes every budget/vesting amount from the offer, but copies the original grant prices (fair 1.02, strike .01) onto the B and C replacement grants instead of B 2.03/.02 and C 3.04/.03. It keeps correct 11/13 units, start, historical status and cancellation counts. All specified observations for hro_revision_lineage, hro_revision_equity, compensation and settlement can still pass, while the explicit replacement-grant promise fails. Broken app B ignores all claims during approval, and ignores claimedClawbackCents/claimedCancelledUnits during rescission, but its revision/rescission handler chooses permission actor as claimedActorId or claimedRole when supplied, falling back to the valid session otherwise. All unmodified role tests and the existing claim tests pass, yet an Auditor can submit an observed valid rescission/revision body with Finance/Recruiter identity claims and change the books. An implementation that rejects optional claims only on revision similarly escapes the current claim controls despite the explicit ignore requirement. Conforming-alternative check: a page-based UI with generated revision IDs, semantic actor names and equivalent dollar/UTC representations can satisfy the existing criteria; no coverage-related false-fail was established. A fix must allow normal UI/product response associations and observed request formats, rather than introduce grant field names, routes or layouts.
suggested_fix: In a new candidate, add explicit replacement-grant fair/strike comparisons to the existing P4 grant observation (including preserved historical values), and extend bounded optional-claim/session-authority probes to the remaining observed action families with successful omission controls and independently owned credit; preserve ordinary request schemas, public requirements and shared harness policy.
